correctness.rationale: The fine nodal slopes 3, 0, −1/4, −1/2 are strictly decreasing at the knots. The fine score vanishes by construction and the log-normalizer's hat covariance is positive definite modulo constants. For the full log-concave class, restriction to the data interval and replacement by the secant interpolant through the log values at the sites cannot increase the normalizing integral; positive mass outside or a positive gap from the interpolant on a set of positive measure makes the likelihood comparison strict. This proves uniqueness of the normalized density (up to null sets). Coarse hat moments are exactly the corresponding fine-density moments, since every coarse hat is its own fine-grid interpolant. An independent rational integration using the Bernstein expansion of each affine power enclosed the three coarse score coordinates at the trial point (approximately 5.096e−9, −4.360e−9 and −2.799e−9); each interval lies inside (−10⁻⁶,10⁻⁶). Direct integration of the centered Gram matrix reproduced leading minors 27/80, 457/7200, 257/108000 after subtracting I/10. The density lower bound 1/40 on the radius-1/100 ball multiplies the Lebesgue variance lower bound (minimize the squared deviation over constants), yielding Hessian >I/400. The objective increases by more than 21/200000000 on the sphere, giving an interior critical point, unique globally by strict convexity. The slope jump is strictly greater than 488249/2500000 after bounding the trial-point displacement, and normalization does not change the jump. Replay: python /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 2.

value.rationale: The witness answers a precise published question about a natural knot-deletion heuristic. It shows that even starting with strictly decreasing slopes at every fine interior knot does not ensure a concave unrestricted reduced fit, and the failure can occur at a retained knot away from the removed one. The exact certificate resolves that substantive issue without a numerical concavity tolerance or a change of weights.
residual_risks: Does not classify which coarsenings preserve concavity or cover higher dimensions.
